blocks.text: The Little Black Gallery announced the publication of the new photo book Garden of Good by Tyler Udall .

The forces that drive Tyler Udall’s work are a combination of his own sexual identity and the evolving societal shifts toward the acceptance and understanding of the LGBTQ+ community. His undeniably personal and emotionally compelling photographs are shaped by the familiarity the artist has with his subjects, most of whom are friends and past lovers.
When I was 12, I left home to study ballet.

I think it’s safe to say that I grew up in the performing arts – surrounded by people pushing their bodies, working hard, longing for something just out of reach, and constantly trying to balance staying in complete control with completely falling apart. Growing up in this kind of environment gave me a strange mix of intimacy and isolation. Through circumstance and necessity, you form a kind of chosen family. As students, you are around each other 24hrs a day, but the very system that brought you together will also tear you apart the moment someone seemingly more valuable appears.
To survive, we learned to split – to become one thing in the spotlight and another when we’re alone. That fracture between the performer and the private self has stayed with me ever since.

All these years later, I still find myself surrounded by performers; dancers, actors, musicians, strippers, acrobats, drag queens, adult film performers… the list goes on. Their mediums might differ, but they all share a common instinct – to create and inhabit (and in some instances weaponize) an alternative version of themselves. Chameleons and their alter-egos. One highly introverted friend of mine becomes a feral animal as soon as she steps on stage. Another erudite friend morphs into pure spectacle as soon as he is being filmed. Curiously, a drag queen friend of mine remains eerily unchanged despite his incredibly extreme transformations.
The boundary is rarely, if ever, clear.

As an emerging photographer, Tyler Udall (b 1979) has already made a big impact in the world of photography exhibiting his work worldwide. He has published three previous books: August 2009–August 2010 (OH WOW Gallery, 2010), Auguries of Innocence (Armour Press, 2015), and I AM (The Little Black Gallery, 2019).

Based in London in the early 2000s, Udall was Senior Fashion Editor at Another Man, Another Magazine, and Dazed & Confused, and was involved in creating iconic covers of Kate Moss, Kirsten Dunst, Tilda Swinton and Natalie Portman. He moved to New York as Creative Director for the agency Fred and Associates, where he teamed up legendary fashion greats with world leading artists. Udall is currently Fashion Director at the Blanche Macdonald Centre in Vancouver – Canada’s top fashion school.

Tyler Udall : Garden of Good 25cm x 20cm 140 pages 98 images Foiled softcover, thread sewn Edition of 300 Edited by Ghislain Pascal Published by The Little Black Gallery Designed by Studio Kunze Printed on FSC, chlorine & acid free paper in the UK Price $75 / £55
Garden of Good by Tyler Udall is available from www.boysboysboys.org
